examples.reason: All candidates in the group have canonical mathematical cosine below the threshold; the conservative box/norm envelope upper bound is also below it. Runtime use still requires outward-rounded f32 proof.
The dot upper bound is negative, so the largest candidate norm gives the least-negative and therefore conservative cosine upper bound.
Positive numerator plus zero lower norm bound cannot produce a useful finite cosine upper bound; refine or score members individually.
Strict upper-bound < kth threshold is required; equality and interval overlap cannot prune.

invariants: Every candidate component must be inside the declared admitted ContinuousHV profile.
Coordinate minima/maxima must cover every eligible member of the pinned group generation.
Norm-squared interval must contain the canonical candidate norm-squared for every group member.
The cosine upper-bound branch uses minimum denominator for a nonnegative dot upper bound and maximum denominator for a negative dot upper bound.
A checksum binds synopsis bytes but does not prove extrema or norm bounds are correct.
Runtime pruning requires directed/outward rounding matching the canonical f32 score contract.
Mixed-eligibility groups require an eligibility-homogeneous synopsis or per-item refinement before payload access.
Equality, numerical uncertainty, stale metadata or invalid ranges cause continued scanning or fail-closed fallback.
nonclaims: No HME implementation or runtime benchmark is represented.
The arithmetic examples are not a floating-point proof.
Group box pruning, vector approximation, VA-files and metric-tree bounds are established prior art; HME novelty is an empirical HDC-specific adaptation only if demonstrated.
